title: Read a tiny CSV
summary: CSV stores rows as text separated by commas. read_csv can read it from a file or, here, an in-memory text buffer.
introduction: CSV stores rows as text separated by commas. read_csv can read it from a file or, here, an in-memory text buffer. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: CSV stores rows as text separated by commas. read_csv can read it from a file or, here, an in-memory text buffer.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

from io import StringIO
small = pd.read_csv(StringIO("item,count\nbook,2\npen,3\n"))
print(small["count"].sum())
blocks.title: Read a tiny CSV

blocks.text: The result is 5. The two count values are added after pandas reads the text as a table.
